output.brief: The buffering is almost certainly caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not by the new CDN. Version 5.2 went live in Kestria (the canary market) on 9 Oct, the same day as the CDN cutover. It cut the startup buffer from 10 s to 4 s and allows quality switch-ups after 2 s, which makes stalls far more likely. Session data shows 5.2 TVs stalling 5.9% of viewing time. Every other client, on the same ISPs and the same Tessaline CDN, sits at about 0.6–0.7%. Employee test TVs served by Corvane showed the same problem (5.7% vs 0.6%) before launch. That rules out the CDN, ISP congestion and the handball launch, whose match nights were no worse. Do not send the breach notice, withhold fees or switch back, and do not mute the alert. Instead, revert the abr_v2 remote-config settings for Kestria to the 5.1 values (about an hour, no new build), and hold the 20 Nov wider rollout until it is fixed. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard when the pipeline allows. The link between buffering and the rise in cancellations is unproven, because the 1 Oct price rise is a competing explanation. Check the exit survey before offering anyone a free month.
